findings.fact: The client presents a terminal through C_BaseTerminal's model-bound character texture, not a named VGUI terminal panel. Its default 36x24 screen is a 1,728-byte array of 864 two-byte character/style cells beginning at +0x7b4.
findings.evidence: Factory/constructor 0x100c6910/0x100c6b30 allocates 0xf20 bytes, initializes 0x1b0 dwords to 0x20202020, and installs vtable 0x102334ac. RefreshTexture 0x100c7720 creates a 512x512 client-effect texture named monitor; RasterizeTexture 0x100c77f0 converts the cell buffer, palette, cursor and glyph table into its pixels.
findings.consequence: Faithful presentation needs a character-cell terminal surface attached to the computer screen; the modern renderer may change, but terminal state must not be modeled as only a modal menu.

findings.fact: C_BaseTerminal edits the command line locally and sends only hackcmd commands to the server. Normal Enter sends hackcmd plus the line, Escape sends hackcmd quit, Ctrl-C sends hackcmd break, and raw-character mode sends hackcmd %c.
findings.evidence: Client vtable 0x102334ac slot 25 resolves to KeyInput 0x100c7090. The body gates on replicated m_bInUse, performs insertion/deletion/cursor movement against the cell buffer, enforces m_nMaxInput, and emits the four hackcmd forms. InsertCharacter 0x100c8060 mutates two-byte screen cells.
findings.consequence: The server remains authoritative for command meaning, while the client owns immediate line editing, cursor behavior and local keystroke feedback.

findings.fact: m_HackFlags bit 0x4 selects raw-character transport, bit 0x1 selects continue/acknowledge input, and bit 0x8 enables local keystroke sound; m_bAllowDirKeys gates cursor navigation.
findings.evidence: KeyInput 0x100c7090 tests +0xf10 bits 4, 1 and 8, +0xf0d direction-key permission, +0xf14 maximum input, and +0xf18 keystroke sound. Server 0x10219120 clears bits 1 and 4; 0x10219240 sets bit 4 and 0x10219270 sets bit 1.
findings.consequence: These replicated flags are protocol state, not presentation-only decoration.
